rounds.proof_sketch: K=4096, BLOCK_SIZE=16. Tiles: ceil(4096/16)=256, so t∈[0,255]. A_col = t*16 + threadCol. Max A_col = 255*16+15 = 4095 < K=4096. The condition A_col==K is never reached, so A_col<K and A_col<=K always evaluate identically.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the boundary check from A_col < K to A_col <= K. This would only matter when A_col equals exactly K, which would be an out-of-bounds access. However, with K=4096 being exactly divisible by BLOCK_SIZE=16, the loop iterates exactly 256 times (t from 0 to 255), and the maximum A_col value is 255*16+15=4095. Since A_col never reaches 4096, both conditions always evaluate to true for all valid thread/tile combinations. The mutation is semantically equivalent under these fixed dimensions.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable with fixed shapes. The mutant would only differ if K were not divisible by BLOCK_SIZE (e.g., K=4097), but shapes are fixed at K=4096 which is exactly divisible by 16.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for tiled GPU kernels should include test cases where dimensions are NOT multiples of the tile/block size to exercise boundary-handling code paths. With K=4097 instead of 4096, this mutation would cause out-of-bounds memory reads and produce detectably different results.
